comparator.academicYear: 2024-2025 official course-and-credit catalogue (the most recent complete formal Bachelor Biomedical Sciences course catalogue accessible to available tools; the curriculum.maastrichtuniversity.nl portal that normally hosts the current-year edition of this catalogue could not be reached by available tools, and no 2025-2026 or 2026-2027 edition, and no Onderwijs- en Examenregeling specific to Biomedische Wetenschappen for any year, could be located through reasonable search of maastrichtuniversity.nl), independently corroborated by the current official programme overview and courses-and-curriculum page content for the Fall-2026 entrant cohort (checked 2026-09-28)
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed primarily from the official Bachelor Biomedical Sciences 2024-2025 course-and-credit catalogue (s2: 'Bachelor Biomedical Sciences', maastrichtuniversity.nl/file/bachelor-biomedical-sciences-2024-2025pdf), which lists every BBSxxxx course offered under the programme with its exact OSIRIS code, ECTS credits, period, prerequisite structure (implicit in the running-text course descriptions cross-referencing earlier courses) and compulsory/restricted-choice status. This is the most recent standalone formal course catalogue for this exact target accessible to available tools; the curriculum.maastrichtuniversity.nl subdomain that normally hosts the current-year 'Courses & curriculum' page returned a DNS/policy failure to every fetch attempt, and no OER (Onderwijs- en Examenregeling) specific to Biomedische Wetenschappen could be located through reasonable search of maastrichtuniversity.nl (searches for 'oer' + 'biomedische wetenschappen'/'biomedical sciences' 2025-2026 returned only OERs for other universities' unrelated Biomedische Wetenschappen programmes, e.g. Utrecht, Leiden and Radboud). Its structure is independently corroborated by current official programme-overview and courses-and-curriculum page content (s0, s1, s3, checked 2026-09-28), which describe the same three-year structure in the same words as the catalogue implements: 'you start out by following mandatory courses, followed by several electives and a minor. You conclude the programme by writing a thesis'; 'the first two semesters form the foundation of the programme' (genetics, cells and tissues, organ/organism physiology and development, research methods and statistics); 'in the third semester we address the immune system, postnatal development and ageing, but also modern imaging techniques'; and 'at the end of the third semester, you can begin to tailor your degree programme to your own requirements, and as of the fourth semester, you can place particular emphasis on certain aspects by selecting courses that fit your interests and ambitions', which the catalogue's own P4-P6 elective structure and Year-3 minor menu formally implement. Year 1 (60 EC) is entirely compulsory and shared: BBS1001 The LEGO Bricks of Life (7), BBS1002 Homeostasis and Organ Systems (7, folding in its paired 0-EC BBS1102 Practicals, which the catalogue lists as a separate 0-credit assessment component of the same course rather than a separately creditable unit), BBS1004 Brain, Behavior and Movement (7), BBS1005 Human Genetics, Reproduction and Prenatal Development (7, folding in its paired 0-EC BBS1105 Practicals on the same basis), BBS1003 Introduction to Statistical Methods for Data Analysis (5), BBS1008 Philosophy in Action I (2), BBS1006 Critical Appraisal of Biomedical Publication (5), plus nine year-long longitudinal competence components (Communication & Cooperation MSF I 4, Scientific Writing I 4, Presenting I 1, Diversity I 1, Professional Behaviour MSF I 3, Professional Development I 3, Laboratory Practice I 2, Practical Skills Exam 1, Calculation Test 1); these period (40 EC) and longitudinal (20 EC) subtotals sum to exactly 60 EC as the catalogue's own period/year structure lays them out. Year 2 (60 EC) opens with three further compulsory courses in periods 1-3 (BBS2001 Threats and Defence Mechanisms 6, BBS2002 From Cradle to Grave: Development, Ageing and Disease 6, BBS2003 Non-invasive Techniques in Biomedical Research 5 = 17 EC) plus the year's own nine longitudinal competence components (26 EC), leaving exactly 17 EC (60-17-26=17) to be filled from period 4, 5 and 6, each of which the catalogue lists as two parallel 6- or 5-EC content modules covering the same weeks with no official name distinguishing them as a formal 'route' or 'track' (P4: Human Intermediary Metabolism 6 EC or Cell Signaling 6 EC; P5: Biorhythms in Homeostasis 6 EC or Neuromuscular Control of Movement 6 EC; P6: Systems Biology 5 EC or Allometry 5 EC), i.e. a genuine restricted-choice elective structure (choose one per period) rather than a named specialisation, exactly matching the 6+6+5=17 EC still required. Because current official evidence confirms only this generic restricted-choice elective structure and no formally named route, no comparator.route is recorded (Section 2.1: preserve the structure generically and leave the route unspecified). Applying the Section 2.1 neutral tie-break for an unavoidable instantiation choice (least specialised/most general option, since neither official page names one option as more representative and UCR fit was not used as a criterion), Cell Signaling was selected over Human Intermediary Metabolism as the more general, cross-cutting mechanistic module (signal transduction underlies the aetiology of many diseases, versus metabolism's narrower nutritional-biochemistry focus); Biorhythms in Homeostasis was selected over Neuromuscular Control of Movement as the module that most directly extends the shared first-year Homeostasis and Organ Systems course's general regulatory-systems content, versus the narrower sports/movement-specific focus of the alternative; and Systems Biology was selected over Allometry as the broader, integrative data-and-pathway-analysis module, versus the narrower scaling-relationships focus of the alternative. Year 3 (60 EC) comprises a further 30 EC of compulsory core (BBS3004 The Core of Biomedical Sciences, a six-week research-lab immersion project, 6; BBS3007 Philosophy in Action III 2; BBS3051 Professional Development III 2; BBS3006 Thesis 20, folding in its paired 0-EC BBS3005 Internship and 0-EC BBS3008 Defence, which the catalogue lists as the same twelve-week internship/thesis/defence sequence assessed as one 20-EC unit) plus a genuine 30-EC minor built from the catalogue's own menu of BBS30xx specialisation modules (four parallel 12-EC period-1 options, four parallel 12-EC period-2 options, converging on one shared 6-EC period-3 Critical Review of a Biomedical Intervention module), again a restricted-choice structure rather than a named track, corroborated by the official description that students 'combine modules into their own minor package'. Applying the same neutral least-specialised tie-break among the sixteen possible period-1/period-2 pairings, Immune Responses in Health and Disease (12) and Infection and Immunity (12) were selected together with Critical Review of a Biomedical Intervention (6) as the minor package: unlike the alternative period-1/period-2 options (Diet Nutrition and Health, Neurosciences and Control, Pharmacological Interventions, Physical Activity and Health, Omics Technologies, Environmental Sustainability and Human Health), which each commit to one narrower applied specialism, this pairing most directly and generally extends the shared, fully compulsory Year-2 Threats and Defence Mechanisms course's own immunology/infection content rather than branching into a narrower nutritional, pharmacological, neuroscientific, exercise-physiological or environmental-toxicological specialism, and is independently reinforced by the target's own programme-interest evidence for the immune system and infection/inflammation (rows 5575, 5576). Every component's exact EC weight is taken directly from the catalogue's per-course ECTS-credit field; the year-1, year-2 and year-3 subtotals each sum to exactly 60 EC. Voltijd delivery starting once yearly in September (confirmed by the official overview page and by the catalogue's own September-start period dates) matches the fixed Fall-2026 UCR cohort.

alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to the Bachelor Biomedical Sciences: a molecular/cellular and organ-systems biomedical core (cell biology, physiology, biochemistry, genetics, anatomy, laboratory technique) combined with the disease side of the programme's own identity (epidemiology, infection & immunity, pharmacology, mechanisms of disease), reinforced by the psychology of health, development and ageing, and by the programme's own methods training (statistics, data science, imaging-technique analysis, qualitative methods, critical appraisal, research ethics and scientific communication) -- reproducing the programme's own combination of biological foundations, disease mechanisms, pharmacology and research-methods training, while leaving the reproduction/embryology dimension, a dedicated clinical-imaging course, a supervised in-lab research placement and the specialist immunology-minor depth genuinely unmatched, since UCR offers no equivalent placement-based thesis or that level of specialist immunology.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is dominated by UCR's biomedical/life-science cluster (11 of 24: Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Molecular Cell Biology, Human Physiology, Biochemistry, Life Science Laboratory, Molecular Pathology & Genetics, Epidemiology & Public Health, Functional Anatomy, Pharmacology, Infection & Immunity and Mechanisms of Disease), reinforced by a psychology/behavioural/neuroscience cluster addressing the human-development, mental-health and brain dimensions of health and disease (6 of 24: Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Abnormal Psychology, Advanced Research Seminar, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Neurobiology) and a research-methods/ethics/communication thread (6 of 24: Research Methods & Statistics, Introduction to Data Science, Image Processing & Computer Vision, Qualitative Research Methodology, Ethics, The Art of Rhetorical Communication) plus PPD. The label names molecular and cellular mechanisms first for the dominant life-science anchor, health and disease second because the whole curriculum is organised around it, and pharmacology third because it is both a strong, distinctly evidenced disease-mechanism/treatment thread and a full course in its own right, mirroring the programme's own combination of molecular/cellular biology, disease/pathology and pharmacology content.

alternatives.concept: A genuinely different second UCR route evidenced by the target's own stable study-direction row naming biomedical entrepreneurship (5585): a programme that studies the science of health and disease only far enough to ground it (molecular/cell biology, physiology, biochemistry, genetics/pathology, pharmacology, infection & immunity), then applies UCR's full available entrepreneurship, business, finance, law and leadership curriculum to translating biomedical research into marketable diagnostics, therapeutics and health ventures -- studying how biomedical science becomes innovation and enterprise, rather than studying the science and its clinical/behavioural context for its own sake as in the closest match.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is dominated by UCR's entrepreneurship, business and economics cluster (14 of 24: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Research Methods & Statistics, Accounting & Corporate Finance, Consumer Product Design, Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Strategy & Digital Transformation, Market Research, International Business & Governance, Personal Leadership, Transnational Business Law, Money Banking & Finance, Leadership & Diversity Management, Introduction to Economics and Public Economics), grounded in a reduced but substantive biomedical-science foundation (7 of 24: Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Molecular Cell Biology, Human Physiology, Biochemistry, Molecular Pathology & Genetics, Pharmacology, Infection & Immunity) plus Introduction to Data Science, The Art of Rhetorical Communication and PPD. The label names biomedical innovation and entrepreneurship first for the dominant business cluster's applied focus, and translating life science into enterprise second because the retained biomedical foundation exists specifically to ground that translation in real scientific content rather than to teach the discipline for its own sake.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The closest match retains a comprehensive 11-course biomedical/life-science core plus a 6-course psychology/behavioural/neuroscience cluster addressing the clinical and developmental context of disease. This alternative goes materially further: it shares only 10 of 24 courses with the closest match (Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Molecular Cell Biology, Human Physiology, Biochemistry, Molecular Pathology & Genetics, Pharmacology, Infection & Immunity, Research Methods & Statistics, Introduction to Data Science, The Art of Rhetorical Communication -- a deliberately retained grounding, since a defensible 'biomedical' entrepreneurship concept must still be built on real biomedical content) and replaces the remaining 14 of the closest match's courses (Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Epidemiology & Public Health, Functional Anatomy, Neurobiology, Life Science Laboratory, Abnormal Psychology, Ethics, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Image Processing & Computer Vision, Qualitative Research Methodology, Advanced Research Seminar, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Mechanisms of Disease, Qualitative Research Methodology) with 14 UCR entrepreneurship, business, finance, law and leadership courses entirely absent from the closest match. This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from studying and researching disease and its clinical/psychological context directly to studying how biomedical discoveries are financed, developed, marketed and governed as products and ventures, and the two alternatives differ in 14 of 24 courses each way (105 EC each way), comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum.

progressionAssessment.rationale: HCBGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precedes Molecular Cell Biology (semester 2), Human Physiology and Biochemistry (semester 3), Life Science Laboratory and Infection & Immunity (semester 4), Molecular Pathology & Genetics and Pharmacology (semester 5), and Mechanisms of Disease (semester 6), all of which formally require it, as well as Functional Anatomy (semester 2), which also formally requires it. HCBGATE102 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precedes Abnormal Psychology (semester 4) and Advanced Research Seminar and Lifespan Developmental Psychology (semester 6), which formally require it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Gateway and level-1/level-2 foundational courses (Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Epidemiology & Public Health, Molecular Cell Biology, Functional Anatomy, Neurobiology, Research Methods & Statistics, Human Physiology, Biochemistry, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Image Processing & Computer Vision) are concentrated in semesters 1-3, and level-3 advanced work (Infection & Immunity, Molecular Pathology & Genetics, Pharmacology, Mechanisms of Disease, Advanced Research Seminar, Lifespan Developmental Psychology) is concentrated in semesters 4-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match directly owns ten generator-eligible rows describing the programme's own biological, disease-mechanism, pharmacological and research-methods identity (5567, 5568, 5569, 5577, 5579, 5580, 5581, 5582, 5583, 5584). These describe the programme's own general biomedical-science identity rather than an independent substantive direction, and are therefore substantively covered by the closest match's own core concept rather than forced into a residual candidate. The two remaining generator-eligible rows are both Stable study direction rows naming distinct non-laboratory career directions: biomedical entrepreneurship (5585) and science education and communication (5586). Biomedical entrepreneurship passes all four gates: it is evidence-backed by a target-specific Stable study direction row; it has a clear organising logic (translating biomedical science into innovation and enterprise rather than studying disease and its clinical/behavioural context for its own sake); it is substantively distinct, replacing 14 of the closest match's 24 courses (105 EC) with UCR's full available entrepreneurship/business/finance/law/leadership curriculum while retaining only the biomedical grounding the concept itself requires; and it is mechanically feasible against the enriched course database, with eight distinct level-300 courses and a pairwise difference of 14 courses (105 EC) against the closest match. Production therefore includes it as the second alternative. Science education and communication was independently assessed and rejected: UCR has a substantial Communication cluster (six MCCCOMM courses) but no education, pedagogy or teacher-training curriculum of any kind, so a full 24-course programme evidencing 'teaching biomedical science' cannot be built without reducing most non-PPD courses to generic-breadth or merely-adjacent justifications for the missing education half of the direction, which Section 2.2 forbids; a communication-only reduction of the direction would in turn not be substantively distinct from the communication and marketing content already present as a complementary thread within the closest match (The Art of Rhetorical Communication) and the second alternative (Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Strategy & Digital Transformation), so it would not represent a genuinely separate, evidence-proportionate third organising concept either. This is recorded as a feasibility failure. No further generator-eligible evidence remains: every generator-eligible row is now owned by either the closest match or the second alternative, and no unclustered generator-eligible row or coherent combination of curricular-topic support-only rows remains available to organise an independent third concept without duplicating one of the two included directions or relying on an omnibus residual bucket. Production therefore stops at two alternatives and records insufficient-evidence as the stopping reason for a third.

notes.text: Both UCR alternatives include substantial study of infection, immunity and disease mechanisms. The Bachelor Biomedical Sciences programme additionally includes a specialist Immune Responses in Health and Disease and Infection and Immunity minor package (24 EC) and a supervised, in-lab research internship culminating in a thesis. UCR students can instead combine Infection & Immunity, Mechanisms of Disease and Pharmacology (and, in the second alternative, UCR's standardised Optional independent research opportunity), but UCR offers no supervised in-lab research placement, dedicated clinical-imaging training or specialist immunology-minor depth of that kind.

The Bachelor Biomedical Sciences programme organises its final year primarily around a specialist biomedical minor and a supervised thesis-based research internship. The second UCR alternative instead organises the equivalent profiling space around translating biomedical science into innovation, entrepreneurship and enterprise, retaining only a reduced shared biomedical-science foundation. The two programmes therefore cover related biomedical-science ground through substantially different curricular structures in their final stage rather than one reproducing the other course by course.
